D.treatment: IHEs with at least 20 TRGP-funded residents
D.comparison: IHEs with fewer than 20 TRGP-funded residents

O.outcome_detail: meeting the suggested cohort-size threshold for economies of scale

cells.quote: Some experts suggest that IHEs need a cohort of around 20 residents to achieve the economies of scale that can help support sustainable and affordable residency programs. This threshold helps IHEs meet minimum class sizes and fund dedicated residency staff. However, even when all self-reported residents are included, regardless of TRGP funding, only 10 of the 24 IHEs with at least one TRGP-funded resident enrolled at least 20 residents.
cells.note: The study reports a descriptive administrative-data comparison against an expert-suggested threshold; it does not measure whether reaching 20 residents actually produced economies of scale.

cells.quote: Many students were quiet lurkers, who read postings but contributed nothing. A small minority of students seemed to enjoy the Bstatus^ associated with being a visible helper and the notoriety of being an Bexpert^ among their peers.
cells.note: The study reports an observational contrast in engagement during iHelp deployment; no quantitative effect size is printed.

D.treatment: strong instructor promotion, visible online presence, and encouragement of peer help
D.comparison: less instructor promotion, presence, or encouragement

cells.quote: Instructors who strongly promoted the use of the tool, who were visibly present in the online discussions, and who encouraged the peer help model, seemed to engender greater engagement by their students.
cells.note: Observational association from iHelp deployments; the study hedges the finding with “seemed to engender.”
